Topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Slopes to Sensitivities

Target audience: University students (Calculus I beginners)

Section: section_1 — Intuitive Hook: The Velocity Analogy

Lecture lines:
Velocity: From total distance to exact instant.
Imagine a cheetah lunging at a gazelle.
We measure speed at that precise point.
Average speed becomes instantaneous speed.
Calculus reveals the truth of the moment.

Planned animations:
Fade in 'Velocity Gauge' graphic at center (#FFFFFF).
Animate needle movement representing increasing velocity (#FF5733).
Transition 'Velocity Gauge' to a position curve graph (#33FF57).
Highlight the instantaneous slope at a specific point (#F3FF33).
Scale up the slope visualization for clarity (#FFFFFF).

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Visual: The Secant-to-Tangent Transition

Lecture lines:
Consider a simple curve.
Draw a secant line between two points.
Slide the second point toward the first.
The secant converges to a tangent line.
This line defines our instantaneous slope.

Planned animations:
Appear 'Secant Line' connecting two points on a curve (#FFFFFF).
Morph 'Secant Line' as the points draw closer (#FF5733).
Show 'Tangent Line' emerging as the limit (#33FF57).
Label 'Secant' and 'Tangent' with contrasting colors (#F3FF33, #FFFFFF).
Animate transition cycle between secant and tangent states (#FFFFFF).

Section: section_3 — Core Concept: The Derivative as a Local Linear Transformer

Lecture lines:
Derivatives are local linear transformers.
Magnify a curve to see a line.
The derivative is the local magnification factor.
It translates input variations to output changes.
Linear approximation defines the derivative.

Planned animations:
Display linear transformation matrix acting on a vector (#FFFFFF).
Animate vector rotating and scaling (#FF5733).
Show 'Derivative' as the local Jacobian matrix (#33FF57).
Overlay local grid distortion to show linearity (#F3FF33).
Fade in label 'Local Linear Map' (#FFFFFF).

Section: section_4 — Visualizing Sensitivity: The 'What-If' Machine

Lecture lines:
The derivative is a sensitivity gauge.
It amplifies or shrinks input nudges.
Small input change leads to output shift.

Planned animations:
Display function input 'x' and output 'f(x)' (#FFFFFF).
Animate 'x' shifting slightly, observing 'f(x)' change (#FF5733).
Show 'Sensitivity' via slope of the change (#33FF57).

Section: section_5 — Summary & Synthesis

Lecture lines:
Derivatives reveal linear truth in curves.
We turn dynamic change into static ratios.
Zooming in makes complexity manageable.

Planned animations:
Display summary table of derivative concepts (#FFFFFF).
Animate connecting lines between 'Velocity', 'Tangent', and 'Linearity' (#FF5733).
Flash the synthesized conclusion 'Derivative = Local Sensitivity' (#33FF57).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
